A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text and Appendices A-E, including equations, proofs, figures and tables, support reliable comparison and matching across pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original RLHF experiments, including reward trajectories, comparisons across reward models and policies, and correlations with reward increase.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds reward-normalization results in Appendix D.1, Figures 11-12 and Table 9.

M1.justification: The RLHF framework, reward-model construction and RLOO/GRPO procedures are retained. The alternative normalization in v2 is presented as a supplementary experimental condition, without a revised proposed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use AlpacaFarm and UltraFeedback for the same alignment tasks. The added normalization experiment reuses the existing Pythia-1B setup without introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The five on-policy/off-policy training mixtures, perfectly accurate low-variance reward model and ground-truth comparator are retained. Section 4.2 also retains GRM-Gemma-2-2B, GRM-Llama-3.2-3B, RM-Tulu-V2-8B and RM-Gemma-2B. The new experiment uses the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds an otherwise identical Pythia-1B experiment that normalizes training rewards by the square root of average within-prompt initial reward variance, replacing the pooled reward standard deviation for this additional experiment. The original normalization experiments remain.

E4.justification: New Figures 11-12 and Table 9 test whether the relationship between reward-model properties and optimization persists under another normalization scheme. This adds a targeted sensitivity analysis while retaining the existing supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain three-run means and standard-deviation error bars in Figures 2-3 and Pearson/Spearman correlation reporting. No changed repeated-run count, seed disclosure or uncertainty-estimation practice is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds reward trajectories and five correlation rows under alternative normalization. Table 9 reports Pearson correlations of 0.936 between reward variance and proxy-reward increase, and 0.808 between combined variance/accuracy and ground-truth reward increase. Existing numerical table rows and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: The theorem statements and proofs retain their mathematical content. Theorem 4 changes J to J_{t_gamma}, but both versions define it through the same supremum over time up to t_gamma. Added remarks clarify the existing bound and reward construction without revising the derivations.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims that low reward variance can hinder RLHF optimization, accuracy alone does not establish reward-model quality, and effective reward-model choice depends on the policy being aligned.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a qualification that growing Jacobian norms could offset the effect of low reward variance. Appendix D.1 interprets the new experiment as robustness across normalization schemes. Section 6.1 also expands the applicability discussion to general reinforcement-learning environments with softmax policies.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly discloses the fallback chat template [USER]x[ASSISTANT]y[EOS], its special tokens, and the use of existing model templates when available. Appendix D.1 specifies the additional normalization rule. Existing hardware, hyperparameter and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes Foster and Foerster's Learning to reason at the frontier of learnability from Section 6.1 and the bibliography. Research positioning otherwise receives limited refinement. Updated publication entries for RewardBench and Progressive distillation induces an implicit curriculum refer to retained works.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits, adds a reward-scale explanation and clarifying remarks, updates appendix-reference terminology, and adds a NeurIPS 2025 footer. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 11-12 and Table 9 using existing display formats. Original plots are retained: v1 Figures 11-12 become v2 Figures 13-14, and Tables 9-11 become Tables 10-12. Other changes involve relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The explicit normalization-sensitivity experiment provides evidence addressing a robustness question left without a corresponding reported comparison in v1. The Jacobian qualification and newly disclosed chat template also improve interpretation and reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains within the existing study; the core theory, task coverage and original results remain unchanged.
